title: DNA Extraction and Genomic DNA Cleanup Protocol for Soil and Environmental Samples
author: Timothy J Philpott
materials: Procure the following reagents before beginning. Chemical name CAS Molecular weight (g/mol) Sodium phosphate, Na3PO4 7601-54-9 163.94 Guanidium isothiocyanate, GITC 593-84-0 118.16 Sodium chloride, NaCl 7647-14-5 58.44 Tris base 77-86-1 121.136 Ammonium acetate 631-61-8 77.08 Aluminium ammonium sulfate dodecahydrate 7784-26-1 453.33 Guanidine hydrochloride 50-01-1 95.53 Calcium chloride dihydrate 10035-04-8 147.01 Ethanol, 100% 64-17-5 46.07 Isopropanol, 100% 67-63-0 60.10

Procure the following materials before beginning. 2 mL screw cap tubes 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes 2 mL microcentrifuge tubes OR 2 mL collection tubes (lidless) Vortex tube adapter (e.g. Scientific Industries SI-HP524 or other bead-based homogenizer) Silica spin columns (Epoch life sciences, cat. no. 1250F-250) 1.0 mm and 0.7 mm zirconia beads (cat. no. 11079110zx and 11079107zx, respectively, BioSpec Products) Magnetic stand for 1.5-2mL tubes (e.g. Promega cat. no. Z5342) Pipette tips (1000, 200, 100, 20 and 10 uL) *The quality of the spin column is critical, a plastic ‘frit’ is required for support, and the column should have at least 4 silica layers. The epoch columns listed above have been tested with the protocol and perform fairly. Spare columns from Qiagen/Mobio powersoil kits work effectively.

Soil DNA from this protocol is often of poor quality (low 260/230 values) due to GuHCl carryover. This is common even in Qiagen’s powersoil kits, which use similar chemistry. Often DNA cleanup is necessary to improve quality. DNA can be cleaned up using commercial bead kits (e.g. ProNex, AMP-pure), or with a non-commercial (DIY) solid-phase reversible immobilization (SPRI) bead solution. This following is a cleanup procedure that has been tested with a DIY SPRI bead solution. This solution can be used in size-selection protocols, but the protocol below is designed to return DNA fragments of all sizes. Expect a 30% reduction in DNA yield. For difficult samples, I have successfully used 2 or even 3 clean ups on the same sample, reducing elution volume to prevent overly diluting samples. The recipe for the SPRI bead solution can be found here: https://openwetware.org/wiki/SPRI_bead_mix . The SPRI solution recipe has been tested exactly as listed in the previous link, except Sera-Mag Carboxylate-Modified (E7) magnetic beads (Cytiva cat. no. 24152105050250) were used instead of the more expensive speed beads referenced in the recipe. Although Cytiva does notrecommend its beads for purification of genomic DNA, testing revealed good recovery of high molecular weight DNA fragments from a DNA ladder. Before beginning, the bead solution should be brought to room temperature and should be well mixed prior to use. Also, prepare an 85 % (v/v), ethanol solution, being sure to measure water and ethanol separately before combining.
Aspirate ethanol solution once cleared (usually 30 seconds).

steps.title: Prepare 1 M Na₃PO₄ stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 81.97 g Na₃PO₄ in molecular‑biology grade water and bring the volume to 500 mL in a volumetric flask.

steps.title: Prepare 1 M guanidinium stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 59.08 g guanidinium isothiocyanate in molecular‑biology grade water and bring the volume to 500 mL in a volumetric flask.

steps.title: Prepare bead solution
steps.instruction: In a 250 mL Pyrex bottle add 45.25 mL of the 1 M Na₃PO₄ stock and 30.25 mL of the 1 M guanidinium isothiocyanate stock; bring the volume to approximately 200 mL with molecular‑biology grade water, slowly adjust pH to 8.8–9.2 with 5 N HCl, decant into a 250 mL volumetric flask and bring to 250 mL with water, yielding a 181 mM bead solution (181 mM Na₃PO₄, 121 mM Na₃PO₄, guanidinium isothiocyanate pH 8.8‑9.2).

steps.title: Prepare Solution 1 (SDS buffer)
steps.instruction: For 10 mL, weigh 0.0877 g NaCl and 0.6057 g Tris, dissolve in 6 mL molecular‑biology grade water, add 4 mL of 10 % SDS stock, do not autoclave, and adjust pH to 10.75‑11.25.

steps.title: Prepare Solution 2 (ammonium acetate)
steps.instruction: For 25 mL, dissolve 0.2563 g ammonium acetate in 25 mL molecular‑biology grade water.

steps.title: Prepare Solution 3A (Aluminum ammonium sulfate)
steps.instruction: For 100 mL, dissolve 8.16 g aluminum ammonium sulfate dodecahydrate in 100 mL molecular‑biology grade water and adjust pH to 3.1‑3.3 with 5 N HCl.

steps.title: Prepare Solution 3B (Calcium chloride)
steps.instruction: For 100 mL, dissolve 3 g calcium chloride dihydrate in 100 mL molecular‑biology grade water.

steps.title: Prepare 1 M Tris stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 60.568 g Tris in molecular‑biology grade water and bring the volume to 500 mL in a volumetric flask (unadjusted pH).

steps.title: Prepare Solution 4 (GuHCl buffer)
steps.instruction: In a 250 mL Pyrex bottle, dissolve 7.5 mL of the 1 M Tris stock and 119.4125 g guanidine hydrochloride in ~150 mL molecular‑biology grade water, add 22.5 mL isopropanol, and slowly adjust pH to 6.69‑6.72 with 5 M HCl, then bring volume to 250 mL with water.

steps.title: Prepare Solution 5 (Ethanol wash buffer)
steps.instruction: In a 100 mL Pyrex bottle, add 1 mL 1 M Tris pH 7.5 stock, 2 mL 5 M NaCl stock, and 37 mL molecular‑biology grade water; autoclave for 20 min, then add 60 mL 100 % ethanol and confirm pH (final: 10 mM Tris pH 7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 60 % v/v ethanol).

steps.title: Prepare Solution 6 (Tris pH 8.5)
steps.instruction: Prepare 10 mM Tris buffer at pH 8.5 (stock details not given; use as supplied).

steps.title: Prepare bead tubes
steps.instruction: Add 0.25 mL of 0.7 mm beads and 0.25 mL of 1.0 mm beads to each 2 mL screw‑cap bead tube.

steps.title: Warm solutions and weigh sample
steps.instruction: If Solution 1 has precipitated, heat at 60 °C in a dry bath until dissolved; warm Solution 6 at 37 °C in a dry bath. Weigh 200‑225 mg fresh mineral soil (or 100‑150 mg freeze‑dried mineral soil, or 50 mg freeze‑dried forest floor) for each tube.

steps.title: Add bead solution and Solution 1
steps.instruction: To each prepared 2 mL bead tube add 750 µL bead solution and 60 µL Solution 1.

steps.title: Add soil sample
steps.instruction: Add 225 mg of fresh mineral soil (or the optimized amount) to each tube and secure the lid tightly.

steps.title: Homogenize sample
steps.instruction: Secure the tube in a vortex‑Genie homogenizer and vortex at maximum speed for 20 minutes (adjust time for your homogenizer).

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge tubes at 17 000 × g for 2 minutes; transfer the 400‑500 µL supernatant to a clean 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Add Solution 2 and freeze
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL Solution 2 to the supernatant, vortex 5 seconds, then incubate at –20 °C for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Centrifuge and transfer supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 2 minutes at 17 000 × g; avoid disturbing the pellet and transfer up to 600 µL supernatant to a clean 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Add Solution 3A/3B master mix
steps.instruction: Mix equal volumes of Solution 3A and Solution 3B to make a master mix; add 200 µL of this mix to each tube, then incubate at –20 °C for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Centrifuge and transfer supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 2 minutes at 17 000 × g; avoid the pellet and transfer up to 750 µL supernatant to a new 2 mL collection tube.

steps.title: Add Solution 4 and mix
steps.instruction: Shake the tube to mix Solution 4, add 1 200 µL of Solution 4 to the supernatant, pipette‑mix, and let stand for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Load onto spin column
steps.instruction: Load 675 µL of the mixture onto a spin column and centrifuge at 10 000 × g for 1 minute; discard the flow‑through. Repeat this loading step twice more until the entire sample has been processed.

steps.title: Wash column with Solution 5
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL Solution 5 to the silica membrane, let sit 1 minute, centrifuge 30 seconds at 10 000 × g, and discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Wash column with 80 % ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL 80 % (v/v) ethanol, let sit 1 minute, centrifuge 30 seconds at 10 000 × g, and discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Dry column
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the empty column for 1 minute at 10 000 × g to remove residual liquid.

steps.title: Elute DNA with warm Solution 6
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of Solution 6 pre‑warmed to 37 °C onto the membrane, wait 5 minutes for absorption, then centrifuge 30 seconds at 10 000 × g.

steps.title: Check DNA concentration
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration; if yield is insufficient, repeat the wash steps (Solution 5 and 80 % ethanol) as needed.

steps.title: Add SPRI beads
steps.instruction: To each eluate, add 2.5× the sample volume of SPRI bead solution.

steps.title: Vortex and incubate beads
steps.instruction: Vortex the tubes for 15 seconds, incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes; if the solution sticks to tube walls, briefly spin down.

steps.title: Separate beads on magnetic stand
steps.instruction: Place tubes on a magnetic stand for 5 minutes or until beads have clearly separated.

steps.title: Aspirate supernatant
steps.instruction: Using a pipette, carefully aspirate the cleared supernatant, leaving ~5 µL behind if necessary, without disturbing the bead pellet.

steps.title: First ethanol wash
steps.instruction: While tubes remain on the magnetic stand, add 200 µL 85 % (v/v) ethanol (increase volume for larger samples to fully cover beads).

steps.title: Vortex and second ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Vortex each tube for 5 seconds, return to magnetic stand, then add another 200 µL 85 % ethanol, vortex 5 seconds, and aspirate as much ethanol as possible without removing beads.

steps.title: Air‑dry beads
steps.instruction: Allow beads to air‑dry for 10 minutes (or 3‑5 minutes in a 37 °C dry bath); do not overdry – beads should appear slightly glossy, not cracked or streaked when flicked.

steps.title: Resuspend beads in Solution 6
steps.instruction: Remove tubes from the magnetic plate and add 40 µL Solution 6 (10 mM Tris pH 8.5); gently pipette up and down 10 times to homogenize (minimum elution volume 30 µL).

steps.title: Incubate eluate
steps.instruction: Incubate the bead suspension for 5 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Separate beads and collect eluate
steps.instruction: Place tubes back on the magnetic stand for 1 minute, then transfer the clear eluate to a new tube, avoiding bead carry‑over.
